date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the final wilderness journey material across Numbers 20–21.
claims.evidence: Numbers 20–21; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: The exact archaeological or external historical setting of this entire passage has not been independently established.
claims.evidence: Phase 1 Dossier 6 and Phase 2 N6-01 (MacDonald, East of the Jordan, directly inspected): Numbers 20-21, Numbers 33, Deuteronomy 2 and Judges 11 preserve inconsistent Transjordan itineraries, so exact route reconstruction is Debated/Unknown. QA Phase 4 section 5.6: MacDonald ch. 5 read directly (pp. 63-100); no primary archaeological report cited for Tell Hisban, Kadesh or Arnon; Levine Numbers 21-36 (4B) unread.

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

connections.note: Related but differently arranged account of the wilderness journey around Edom.
Related but differently arranged account of the encounters with Sihon and Og.
Jephthah's message retells Israel's passage past Sihon of Heshbon, the battle at Jahaz, and possession from Arnon to Jabbok.
Direct reference to the Num 20 exclusion: Moses must die on Nebo because of the trespass at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, as Aaron died on Mount Hor.
Poetic retrospective: the people angered God at the waters of strife, and it went ill with Moses for their sakes.
Parallel water-from-the-rock account at Rephidim (Massah and Meribah); differs from Num 20 in setting and details, so it is a parallel, not the same event.
